title: Levelwise normalized strict systems and evaluated adjunction interfaces
statement: Let $O$ be a commutative ring, $\lambda\in O$, and $W$ a scheme. On its small etale and pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-etale-site] [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], use ordinary strict semilinear systems of $O/(\lambda^{n+1})$-module sheaves, their unbounded derived category and exact evaluation/derived quotient packages [lem-pur-coefficient-system-derived-comparison] [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Define $\mathscr N_W^\tau$ to be the full subcategory whose actual adjoint derived transitions are all invertible and whose every evaluation is bounded constructible [def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility] of finite Tor amplitude [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude]. The bounds are allowed to depend on $n$. Identify ring-sheaf module levels with fixed-coefficient sheaves using canonical constant scalar restriction [def-coef-constant-scalar-restriction], applied to derived categories as the exact additive functor it is [lem-sfb-constant-scalar-restriction-tensor]. For a compactification $c=(j,p)$ [def-weil-compactifications-refinements] and its actual strict etale compact-support functor [def-per-strict-etale-system-interfaces], the evaluated-adjunction interface consists of an ordinary right adjoint, finite evaluated adjunctions, evaluation isomorphisms preserving their units and counits, the canonical open quotient isomorphism, and a family $b$. Define $q$ by pasting the open quotient map and proper counit mate [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate]. The transition predicate states the two actual adjoint-transition equations and the counit equation characterizing $b$ as the mate of $q$. The strict etale and pro-etale evaluation interfaces retain their actual site-comparison construction data [def-coef-system-site-transport-interfaces].
